[strategy/guidance/security/Application/ref-arch/GUID-SEC-APP-RA-APP-IDENTITY-2.7.32.md#rad-scope]

### RAD Scope

- User-facing authentication flows mediated by the Application Identity Broker
- Token issuance, distribution, and validation lifecycle
- Per-request token validation as a shared capability
- Machine-to-machine authentication using platform-issued identity tokens

[strategy/guidance/security/Application/ref-arch/GUID-SEC-APP-RA-APP-IDENTITY-2.7.32.md#capability-domain-boundary]

### Capability Domain Boundary

Application Identity and Token Security covers the authentication and token validation layer within application architecture. Its upstream boundary is the enterprise identity provider (which authenticates the principal). Its downstream boundary is the authorization evaluation point (which uses validated claims to make access decisions). Enterprise workforce identity management (directory services, MFA enrollment, credential lifecycle) is in scope for the Identity Security domain.

[strategy/guidance/security/Application/ref-arch/GUID-SEC-APP-RA-APP-IDENTITY-2.7.32.md#logical-components]

### Logical Components

| Component | Type | Architectural Role |
|---|---|---|
| Application Identity Broker | ABB Realization — GUID-SEC-APP-ABB-IDBRKR-2.7.26 | Mediates authentication; issues standardized identity tokens |
| Enterprise Identity Provider | External Dependency | Authenticates principals; federation source |
| Token Validation Layer | ABB Realization — GUID-SEC-APP-ABB-TOKVAL-2.7.27 | Validates token signatures, expiry, audience, and claims on each request |
| Authorization Evaluator | Integration — GUID-SEC-APP-ABB-APIAZ-2.7.12 | Evaluates access policy based on validated claims |
| Session Audit Log | Logging Component | Records authentication events and validation failures |

[strategy/guidance/security/Application/ref-arch/GUID-SEC-APP-RA-APP-IDENTITY-2.7.32.md#pattern-1-browser-based-user-authentication-with-session-token]

### Pattern 1: Browser-Based User Authentication with Session Token

**When to use**: Web applications accessed by human users via a browser.

**Logical flow**:

1. User accesses protected resource; application redirects to Identity Broker
2. Broker initiates federation protocol exchange with Enterprise IdP
3. Enterprise IdP authenticates the user and returns an assertion to the Broker
4. Broker issues an application session token and redirects the user back
5. Browser presents the token on each subsequent request
6. Token Validation Layer verifies the token on every request before the request reaches application logic
page_texts.13:
[strategy/guidance/security/Application/ref-arch/GUID-SEC-APP-RA-APP-IDENTITY-2.7.32.md#pattern-2-api-access-with-bearer-token]

### Pattern 2: API Access with Bearer Token

**When to use**: API endpoints accessed by client applications or service-to-service calls.

**Logical flow**:

1. Client application obtains a token (via broker or via platform identity mechanism for service accounts)
2. Client presents the token as a bearer credential in each API request
3. API Gateway or application-layer middleware invokes Token Validation
4. Validated claims are passed to the Authorization Evaluator
5. Authorized requests proceed; invalid or unauthorized requests are rejected with appropriate HTTP status
page_texts.14:
[strategy/guidance/security/Application/ref-arch/GUID-SEC-APP-RA-APP-IDENTITY-2.7.32.md#pattern-3-machine-to-machine-identity-with-platform-token]

### Pattern 3: Machine-to-Machine Identity with Platform Token

**When to use**: Service-to-service calls within the platform where both services have platform-assigned workload identities.

**Logical flow**:

1. Calling service obtains a short-lived platform identity token for its workload identity
2. Service presents the platform token when calling a downstream service
3. Downstream service validates the token using the Token Validation shared capability
4. Validated platform identity claim is used to evaluate whether the calling service is authorized

[strategy/guidance/security/Application/ref-arch/GUID-SEC-APP-RA-APP-IDENTITY-2.7.32.md#deployment-context-considerations]

## Deployment Context Considerations

| Context | Architectural Consideration |
|---|---|
| Cloud-native (Kubernetes) | Platform workload identity tokens (e.g., service account tokens projected into pods) can serve as the machine-to-machine identity token; Token Validation must support this token type |
| Multi-region | Token Validation must use regionally available key material; key endpoint availability is a critical dependency |
| Legacy application integration | Applications that cannot consume bearer tokens may require a token exchange pattern at the integration boundary |

page_texts.16:
[strategy/guidance/security/Application/ref-arch/GUID-SEC-APP-RA-APP-IDENTITY-2.7.32.md#constraints-and-exceptions]

## Constraints and Exceptions

- The Token Validation capability depends on key material availability from the issuing authority; operational resilience of the identity infrastructure is a critical dependency.
- Session token lifetime must be balanced between security (shorter lifetimes) and user experience (longer lifetimes); enterprise session policy must define the acceptable range.
- Token claims required for authorization must be defined by the application team and communicated to the identity broker configuration team before onboarding.
page_texts.17:
[strategy/guidance/security/Application/ref-arch/GUID-SEC-APP-RA-APP-IDENTITY-2.7.32.md#application-onboarding-contract]

### Application Onboarding Contract

Integrating a new application with the Application Identity Broker requires a defined handoff contract between development teams, Security Architecture, and Platform Engineering. Without an explicit contract, claims configuration becomes an ad-hoc dependency that blocks application deployments.

At minimum, the onboarding contract SHALL define:

- Required claims and token usage expectations from the application team
- Security Architecture review criteria for claim scope and least-privilege alignment
- Platform Engineering configuration responsibilities for broker registration and mapping
- Joint validation responsibilities to verify issued tokens satisfy approved claim requirements

Lead-time targets, queue policies, and escalation windows for onboarding are operational parameters and SHALL be defined in jointly governed operational agreements rather than in this architecture document.
